question: How did the supreme lord provide refuge for the serpent-king?
premises: The supreme lord placed the serpent on the seat of his own matted-hair mass.
After that, all hosts of gods held the serpent on their own heads.
The serpent thus received a place of honor and refuge.
inference: The serpent-king was elevated from exile to a position of universal honor through the lord's protection.
uncertainties: The shift from singular refuge on Shiva's head to being held by all gods is compressed and may be symbolic.
plain_english: The supreme lord placed the serpent on the seat of his own matted hair. Then all the hosts of gods bore him upon their own heads.
